label: paragraph_title
text: Paris, September 1

label: text
text: The newspapers fear that the League will henceforth be dominated by Germany—Renter.

label: text
text: The Council has approved Mr. Von Under's modified resolution ceiling, with the Mandates Commission, so as to satisfy the Mandatory Powers in hearing the petitions and in regard to questions to be addressed to the Mandatories Ceiling with the administration of Mandated Territories.

label: text
text:
The Council agreed. In a secret session that there was no need for further enquiry regarding Germany's eligibility. All that remains is the vote of the Assembly, which will be taken on Wednesday afternoon which the Council will resolve on giving a permanent seat to Germany and ask the Assembly on the same day, to add three non-permanent seats. The Council anticipated that the German delegates will leave Berlin in time to arrive for the official welcome on Friday.
The Council of the League in a plenary public session unanimously adopted the report of the Reorganization Committee presented by Faron Fihil and approved the solution designating Germany as a permanent member of the Council to soon as she enters the League.
- Reiden

label: paragraph_title
text: Rugby, September

label: text
text: After the Committee on the Reconstitution of the League Council had yesterday adopted its report for communication to the Council a resolution was moved by Lord Civil and unanimously passed asking the Spanish member to transport to his Government the Committee's arrest hope that they would favourably consider effort made to meet their wishes and waiting as evidence of goodwill concessions made with the object of satisfying the claimants to permanent Council seats. Telegrars from Geneva suggest the likelihood that Spain will temporarily disintegrate herself in the work of the League and will refrain from vetoing in Council the proposal to plot a permanent seat to Germany, British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain and Mr. Briand have telegraphed to General Prime de Rivera urging Spain's presence at the Council meeting. Prime de Rivera replied: "In my modesty I never expected to receive such an honour as that which Your Excellencies' telegram constitutes. My personal inclination would lead me to agree immediately if it were not my duty to watch ever the prestige of my well-beloved Spain, which is relegated to a position inferior to that which she merits and must take refuge in proud abstention."—Reuter

label: paragraph_title

label: paragraph_title
text: Kungby. Septembor 5:

label: text
text: The present week will see Germany's entry into the League of Nations. On Saturday the final technicalities were completed, and the Council unanimous-accepted the report of the Committee on reorganisation.

label: text
text: The Council has thus expressed its clear intention of making Germany the sole permanent addition to its members.

label: text
text:
The Assembly is, of course, the final authority, but the formalities connected with its approval of the Council's decision will probably be completed on Wednesday, so that the German delegation can take its place in the Assembly on Friday.
Although it is believed and hoped that Spain will not resign from the league, she will temporarily accept herself from the proceedings, this decision being announced in a report from General Primo de Rivera to a pressing appeal from Sin Austen Chamberlain in M. Briand, British Wireless Service.

text: "Madrid, September 5. In a long manifesto to the country General de Rivera states that the old Parliamentary regime has proved a failure, not only in Spain but in other countries," He advocates the establishment of a Supreme National Assembly, in which all classes of interests will be justly balanced. He is of opinion that such a body would put an end to intrigues without less of time.—Reuter.

label: doc_title
text: "SAVE YOUR JOBS."

label: text
text:
ADVICE OF WARWICKSHIRE
OWNERS.

label: text
text: At length there is a prospect of a settlement of the protracted coal trouble on lines which, it is hoped, will bring enduring peace to Great Britain's basic industry.

label: text
text: Although the owners are still irrevocably opposed to the principle of a national agreement, holding that the freedom resumed by the districts on the abandonment of control by the Central Council of the Mining Association should be maintained, it is declared that the District Associations of Coal Owners will resist a renewed abrogation of their powers of negotiation and wages settlements. Therefore, if a national wage basis is agreed to between the Government and the miners, it may be necessary to obtain legislative power to impose it.

label: text
text: On the other hand it is possible that such a situation may be created that the coal owners' negotiating Committee may bring influence to bear on the districts to modify their attitude.

label: text
text: "It is noteworthy that the Warwickshire coal owners have notified the miners that a national wage scheme would put them on a level with the lowest paid district and ask them if the reduction is worth fighting for." Save your jobs and let the other districts do the same."—Reuter.

label: text
text:
London, September 5.
The Mining Association represents the Joint Conference between both parties in the dispute.—Reuter.
London, September 5.
Although representatives of the Mining Association and the Cabinet Council Committee are meeting on Monday, the textsof Letters exchanged with the Miners' Department reveal that the Association is theidedly against the miners' desire for a national settlement.

label: text
text: The Secretary of the Association, the Miners' Federation and the Government, declared that the Association had no authority to discuss and negotiate on behalf of District Owners' Associations questions relating to terms of employment with workmen; they, therefore, declined to attend a tripartite meeting. The reply, further to the letter from the Miners' Mining Association secretary, agreed to meet the Cabinet Coal Committee on Monday.—Reuter

label: text
text: The Central Council of the Soviet Labour Unions are transmitting "to the British Mirers' Federation all available sums collected by means of a levy". The members, in addition, advance on account of future levies, a total remittance of three million roubles.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: The Miners' Letter

label: text
text: Late last night the Miners Executive sent a communication to Mr. Churchill, Chancellor of the Exchequer, containing a formula which has enabled the Government to request the mine owners to resume negotiations. The letter to Mr. Churchill, which was signed by Mr. A. J. Cook, the miners' secretary states that the Executive Committee and a special delegate conference of the Miners Federation having again carefully considered the present deadlock in the mining dispute "have resolved to ask you to convene and attend a conference of the Mining Association and Federation. We are prepared to enter negotiations for a new national agreement with a view to a reduction in costs to meet the immediate in costs to meet the immediate necessities of the industry." An official announcement states, "The Government considers that this letter constitutes a basis sufficient to justify them" in requesting the Mining Association to resume negotiations and they are communicating with them accordingly. The Prime Minister is being kept fully informed of the course of

label: text
text: The Miners Executive's letter constitutes a distinct advance upon their previous attitude. The phrase "reduction in labour costs" is sufficiently comprehensive to permit discussion on hours as well as wages and reorganisation of industry. At the moment, however, the statement that the miners are prepared to negotiate for a "new national agreement" is of primary importance in view of the decision of the mine owners not to negotiate nationally and to take separate agreements in districts as the only basis for the settlement of the dispute.

label: text
text: A full conference of mining owners will probably be called to consider the letter from the Government suggesting a reopening of negotiations with the miners' national body.

label: text
text: Owners will be invited and expected not to impede a settlement by rigid adherence to this attitude.

label: text
text: that divergence of view on this aspect of the dispute should prove irreconcilable and Mr. Churchill in the House of Commons on Tuesday suggested as possible "A national settlement within whose ambit district conditions have been properly considered and district arrangements are properly embodied." The next step now lies with the mine owners.

label: text
text: Mr. Ramsay McDonald, leader of the Labour Parliamentary Party, who was, in active consultation throughout yesterday with the Miners' Executive, has expressed great satisfaction at the decision of the Government to take action on the communication from the miners, which he helped to prepare. —British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: Position Reviewed.

label: paragraph_title
text: Rugby, Sept. 5

label: text
text: As a result of the correspondence between the coal owners and the Government Minis Department, representatives of the Mining Association will attend meeting of the Coal Committee of the Cabinet to-morrow to discuss the question of calling a joint conference of the parties to the coal dispute.

label: text
text: The association had in a previous letter informed the Mines Department that they were unable to meet the miners in three-corner conferences to discuss a national agreement as they "had no authority to enter into any discussions of negotiations on behalf of the District Colliery Owners' Associations on questions of terms of employment of workmen."

label: text
text: The general belief is that the insistence of the coal owners to settle terms in the districts and, not on a national basis will not be allowed to block the way to a settlement.

label: text
text:
The Government view that this matter is capable of equitable settlement by a national agreement, with district variations in accordance with the conditions existing in the different apels, was expressed by Mr. Churchill, Chancellor of the Exchequer, in parliament last week.
This view was expressed strongly by the Goal Commission's report, and the negotiation of such an agreement is now the sole limitation placed by the Miners' Executive on the scope of the discussion at the joint conference which they requested Mr. Churchill to convene.

label: text
text: Pesumably the Cabinet Coal Committee, at their meeting with the Mining Association to-morrow will invite that Body to obtain from the District Coal Owners' Associations a mandate to enter upon discussions on a national basis. British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: NOTE TO CHINA.

label: paragraph_title
text:
SOVIET AND MUKDEN WAR
LORD.

label: text
text: Moscow, Sept. 4.

label: text
text: M. Chichigrin has handed the Chinese Charge d'Affaires in Moscow, for transmission to the Chinese Government, a Note protesting against Marshal Chang Tsolin's demand to the Board of the Chinese Eastern Railway to hand over to the Mukden authorities all vessels belonging to the Railway, also a demand for a liquidation of the training department of the Railway and to transfer all schools to the control of the Mukden authorities.

label: text
text: The Note points out that the Government has repeatedly attempted to adjust its differences with the Railway in an amicable spirit, but, for reasons beyond Soviet control, all such attempts have been futile. The Soviet is again ready to enter into the question of all differences, but emphatically protests against the one-sided action of the Chinese Government in violating the essential Treaty rights of Soviet Russia in North Manchuria.

label: text
text: The Soviet awaits the immediate withdrawal of the demand and insights on the submission of the questions through diplomatic channels to both Governments.

label: paragraph_title
text: More Allegations.

label: text
text: The Pravda declares that Chang Tso-lin is determined to cripple the Chinese Eastern Railway violently as the Railway during the last few months carried considerably more traffic than the South Manchurian Railway, which is controlled by the Japanese, whom the Soviet Press accuses of supporting Chang Tso-lin for their own ends.

label: text
text: The paper says that the Soviet will submit no provocation, but will continue a policy exclusively in defence of the workers of Russia and China.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: SWATOW OUTRAGE.

label: text
text: CHINESE EMPLOYEE OF BRITISH FIRM CHAINED.

label: text
text: Swatow, August 23.—Last week was reported the outrage, committed on a leading Chinese British subject by the police here. This has been followed up by a still more dastardly attack upon another man by the strike pickets. The victim in this case is the head Chinese in the employ of Messrs. Bradley and Co., with whom he has been for 30 years. Like other Chinese employees, he, of course, had not been working in the office since the boycott began; but recently, as the firm had business to transact with the Reclamation Bureau, he was given a special official permit to attend the office. In the face of this he was, some days ago, on his arrival at the office, laid hold of by a body of pickets, and carried off to one of their dens, where he has been chained up and kept on the verge of starvation since—in the hope, no doubt, that he will come to the point of paying some huge sum for release from his misery. So much for the value of the pledged word of the official. So much also, alas, for the value of the once boasted British citizenship. So much, again, for the justice which we are assured China is going to met with open hand when extraterritoriality goes. The official position is that Chinese are Chinese, and have no right to call themselves citizens of other countries. It looks as if the British government had decided to take the same view. If so, it is at least due to the Chinese who think they can claim British protection that the government should enlighten them.—“N.C.D.N.”
